scene_text: INT. CHILD'S BEDROOM - NIGHT. A small bedroom, about 5 by 4 metres. A bed against the left wall, a tall wardrobe closet against the back wall, slightly right of centre, its door ajar. MAYA (30s) stands in the middle of the room holding a flashlight, listening. A faint knocking comes from inside the closet. She edges toward it. The knocking stops. Silence. She reaches for the handle — and the closet door bangs open on its own. We want a slow creeping push toward Maya and the closet, then a violent whip to the closet door on the bang.

beats.description: Maya stands mid-room, flashlight beam sweeping the walls, listening.
Faint knocking from inside the wardrobe; Maya freezes, beam snaps to the closet.
Knocking stops. Silence. Maya edges one slow step toward the closet.
Maya reaches for the handle, fingers trembling.
The closet door bangs open on its own; camera whips to the dark interior.

references.moment: Carolyn follows disembodied claps; two hands emerge from the wardrobe.
references.technique: Locked-off wide held on the actor, slow push toward the wardrobe mouth.
references.why: The camera refuses to cut, letting the wardrobe sit at frame's edge so the audience's eye snaps to it exactly when Maya's beam does at t=3s.

references.moment: The camera rushes at Katie, then cuts to her face frozen in the closet.
references.technique: Accelerating push-in, then hard cut to the dark interior.
references.why: This is the t=11s beat — the whip into the black closet interior, where the reveal is a face rather than an empty space.

references.moment: A slow pan across a quiet suburban street, then a 360-degree sweep.
references.technique: Methodical wide-angle 360-degree pan on a Steadicam.
references.why: The unhurried, continuous sweep mirrors Maya's flashlight arc at t=0s and the dread of the single slow step at t=6s — nothing cuts, so nothing is safe.

references.moment: Every cabinet and door in the kitchen flies open at once.
references.technique: Static wide surveillance-style frame; violence happens inside the frame, not through a cut.
references.why: The model for the closet door banging open "on its own" at t=11s — the camera doesn't move, so the door's motion reads as the room acting, not the operator.

techniques.name: Peek around the corner
techniques.effect: the camera itself behaves like an intruder
techniques.move: Camera starts hidden behind a wall or doorframe and slowly leans out to reveal the room.
techniques.rig_notes: Small lateral move plus a slight yaw. Do not intersect the wall prop.
techniques.matched_beat: The closet door bangs open on its own; camera whips to the dark interior. (, )

techniques.name: Pull-back isolation
techniques.effect: loneliness; the character becomes small and vulnerable
techniques.move: Start on a medium close-up, pull straight back and up slightly to a wide.
techniques.rig_notes: Back along the rail axis; watch reach when the camera rises at the far end.
techniques.matched_beat: The closet door bangs open on its own; camera whips to the dark interior. (, )

techniques.name: Rack-focus reveal
techniques.effect: a figure materialises out of the blur behind the hero
techniques.move: Locked or barely moving camera; focus pulls from foreground subject to background threat.
techniques.rig_notes: Almost static; lens-only plus a tiny push.
techniques.matched_beat: The closet door bangs open on its own; camera whips to the dark interior. (, )

techniques.name: Mirror reveal
techniques.effect: the jump scare is behind the character, seen in a reflection
techniques.move: Frame the character in a mirror; push gently or rack focus as a figure appears behind them.
techniques.rig_notes: Keep the camera out of the mirror's reflection line: angle 20-30 degrees off the mirror normal.
techniques.matched_beat: The closet door bangs open on its own; camera whips to the dark interior. (, )

techniques.name: Snap zoom
techniques.effect: shock; a sudden emphasis on a detail
techniques.move: Very fast zoom in on a face or object while the camera stays still.
techniques.rig_notes: Lens-only; no arm movement at all, so it never violates motion limits.
techniques.matched_beat: The closet door bangs open on its own; camera whips to the dark interior. (, )

techniques.name: Handheld panic (simulated)
techniques.move: Small, fast, irregular jitters of 2-6 cm on top of a forward move.
techniques.rig_notes: Many keyframes 0.2-0.3 s apart with tiny offsets; check acceleration limits.
techniques.matched_beat: Maya reaches for the handle, fingers trembling. (, )

shot_list.director_notes: Fix: the simulator flagged S2's easing keyframe again — the 0.35 s move from the wide look_at (2.5, 2.5) to the wardrobe mouth (3.2, 3.4) still asked the rail axis to accelerate 1.0x past limit. I stretched that move to 0.45 s (comfortably past the required 0.41 s) and shifted every later S2 keyframe by +0.10 s, so the snap now lands at t=0.70 and holds to t=1.7 — still inside the 0.2-0.6 s snap window and still carrying the easing beat. Everything else is untouched: same rail line at y=0.35 clear of the Bed, same four shots, same references, same lens choices. The scare is identical — the lens still slams onto the closet mouth the instant the knock lands, it just takes a tenth of a second longer to get there.

shots.name: The Room Refuses to Cut
shots.intent: Establishes the whole room and lets the wardrobe sit at frame's edge, so the audience's eye snaps to it exactly when Maya's beam does at t=3s. The slow drift keeps the dread continuous — nothing cuts, so nothing is safe.
shots.reference_title: The Conjuring (2013) — Carolyn follows disembodied claps; two hands emerge from the wardrobe

shots.name: Beam Snaps to the Closet
shots.intent: The knock lands and the lens alone slams onto the wardrobe mouth — no arm movement, so the scare reads as the room's attention snapping, not the operator's. The easing keyframe 0.45s before the snap keeps the zoom from feeling mechanical while staying inside the acceleration limit.
shots.reference_title: The Ring (2002) — The camera rushes at Katie, then cuts to her face frozen in the closet

shots.name: One Slow Step
shots.intent: Maya edges toward the closet and the frame breathes with her — tiny irregular jitters on a forward creep that make the audience feel her pulse without ever losing the wardrobe in frame. The move tracks her walk so she stays centred as she closes the distance.
shots.reference_title: It Follows (2014) — A slow pan across a quiet suburban street, then a 360-degree sweep

shots.name: The Door Bangs Open
shots.intent: The camera holds dead still while the closet door flies open on its own — the violence happens inside the frame, so the room reads as the actor and the audience has nowhere to look but the dark interior. A tiny push and a focus pull from Maya's hand to the black mouth lands the scare without a cut.
shots.reference_title: Paranormal Activity 2 (2010) — Every cabinet and door in the kitchen flies open at once

violations.suggestion: Route the camera around 'Bed' (pass above it or stay on the near side) or move the rail so the arm does not reach across it.

shot_list.director_notes: We hold the room in one unbroken wide for the first six seconds so the wardrobe sits at frame's edge and the audience's eye snaps to it exactly when Maya's beam does — nothing cuts, so nothing is safe. Then we compress: a slow push that becomes a rush, and finally a locked-off frame where the door's violence happens inside the frame, not through a cut. Every move stays on the rail line at y=0.9, which keeps the arm clear of the bed box and Maya's path while giving us a clean 1.0 m reach to the closet mouth.

violations.detail: The rail axis is asked to accelerate 1.4x past its limit during the move from t=0.00s to t=0.25s.
violations.suggestion: Make that move take at least 0.34s instead of 0.25s (shift every later keyframe by 0.09s), or cut the angle it sweeps by about 27%. Extra keyframes in between do not help; time does.

shot_list.director_notes: Fix: the rail was sitting inside the Bed footprint (Bed spans x 0.0–1.8, y 0.6–2.6), so the pedestal column was colliding with it. I moved the rail to y=0.35 — in front of the bed's near edge at y=0.6, with 0.25 m of clearance for the column and a clean 1.0 m reach to the camera line at y=1.35. That keeps the camera on the open fourth-wall side of the bed, never reaching across it, and still gives a clear sightline to the wardrobe mouth at (3.2, 3.4). All four shots now sit on that single rail line; the arm resets between takes. The plan is unchanged: one unbroken wide for six seconds so the wardrobe lives at frame's edge, then a lens-only snap at the knock, a breathing creep toward the closet, and a locked-off frame where the door's violence happens inside the frame.

notes: Listen up. The scare is the room itself — the wardrobe snaps our attention, not the operator. Rhythm: one unbroken drift, a hard 1.7-second snap zoom on the knock, a short handheld creep with Maya, then dead-still as the door bangs open on its own. Four beats, no cuts, no escape. Safety: the closet door is on a pneumatic release — nobody stands inside its swing arc, and Maya holds her mark until I call it. Three rig revisions are in; no open issues. Let's shoot it.
